title: ATX Bills Jump: Water Hikes, Organics, & More
meeting_type: Austin City Council Special Called Budget Work Session
summary:
*   **Water Rate Increase Proposed:** Austin Water plans a 4.8% rate increase, leading to an average residential bill increase of $4.94 per month. This aims to improve the utility's financial health, bolster cash reserves, and prevent a potential bond rating downgrade.
*   **Drought Restrictions Debate:** Despite recent significant rainfall and lake levels at 75% capacity, Austin Water recommends maintaining Stage 2 water restrictions (one day per week watering), sparking council debate over the ongoing impact on residents' landscaping.
*   **New Organics Waste Program:** Austin Resource Recovery proposes a five-year rollout of a food waste collection program, projecting a cumulative $4.10 per month increase on residential utility bills by 2020 to achieve higher diversion rates from landfills.
*   **Rising Waste Management Fees:** Residential customers also face an additional $1.70 per month base fee increase from Austin Resource Recovery to cover rising operational costs and depleting fund balances, alongside new investments in fleet technology ($1.5M) and expanded downtown litter cleanup services.

topics.sentence: Our major accomplishments in this past physical year, we engaged in a waste composition study of the material going to the landfill and observed some valuable insights on types of recyclables that are going to the landfill that we need to capture in our blue carts.
